dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Yes, hello. Um, I am calling about water. Water is coming out from a pipe, at the curb, and it is, how you say, it is going on the sidewalk and now it is ice.
Okay. Water coming out of a pipe at the curb and freezing on the sidewalk. Can I get the address where you're seeing that?
Yes. Two fifty-one Broadway. In the North End. My shop is there, so I see it every day, from the window.
Two fifty-one Broadway, got it. And you said it's your shop. Is the pipe right in front of your building?

Yes, right in front, at the edge of the street. It is a pipe, not big, but the water, it runs, runs, all the time. Today is not raining. Yesterday not raining. Nothing. Is dry. So this is not from the storm.
Right, so it's running in dry weather. Has it been going for a few days, or longer than that?

Um, [pause] more than one week. Maybe ten days. I called one time before, I think, to somebody, but nobody comes. I see nobody. And every morning the sidewalk is like a, a glass. Slippery. A customer almost fall down this morning.

Oh, no. I'm sorry about that. Let me make sure I have this right. About ten days of water running from a pipe at the curb, no rain, and it's freezing into ice on the sidewalk in front of your shop. Is that it?

Yes, yes, exactly. And, one more thing. The water, it goes down the sidewalk, and now it goes toward the neighbor. He has a garage, next door. The water is going to the garage door. If it freeze there, or if it goes inside, is a problem for him.
Okay, so it's moving along the curb toward the neighbor's garage. Is it already reaching the door, or is it close?
Is close. Maybe, um, two meters? Three? It makes a little river and then ice. I put salt, but the water comes again, so the salt is finished.
That makes sense, the salt won't hold up against constant water. Do you know if it's clear water, or does it look like it's coming from a drain or a broken line?

It is clear. No smell. It comes out from the pipe, the little one in the curb, not from the grate. I don't know if it is a water pipe from the street or from the drain. I am not the expert. I only know it does not stop.

That's okay, you don't have to know. We'll send somebody to look at it and figure out whose it is. Let me put this in as a drainage problem with ice on the sidewalk, and I'll note the garage next door so they know it's urgent.
Yes, please. Because I pay my taxes, my business, and this is ten days. I am a little tired to call. Somebody must come and see.
I understand, and you're right to keep calling. Can I get a name and a number in case the crew needs to reach you?
Yes. Luz Quintero. Q-U-I-N-T-E-R-O. The number is four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-five-four.
Luz Quintero, Q-U-I-N-T-E-R-O, four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-five-four. Did I get that right?
Yes, perfect. Thank you.
Okay. And are you at the shop most of the day?

Yes, from eight to six. Tomorrow also. And Saturday I open too. Um, I want to ask, do the crews work on weekends? Because if nobody comes tomorrow, then Saturday, Sunday, the ice is there all the time.

Some crews do come out on weekends for urgent things, like ice and water on a walkway. I can't tell you for certain someone will be there Saturday, but I'm marking this as a safety hazard so it gets looked at as soon as they can get to it. Most likely a crew will see it tomorrow.
Okay. Tomorrow, I hope. Because today, I already almost have an accident in my store entrance.
Understood. In the meantime, if you have sand or more salt, putting some down near your door will help with footing. And maybe a cone or a sign if you have one, so people see the ice.
Yes, I have a sign. The yellow one, for wet floor. I will put it outside. [pause] But I think the city should fix the pipe, not me with the sign.

You're right, that's on us to look at. So I have two fifty-one Broadway, North End, a pipe at the curb running about ten days in dry weather, ice on the sidewalk, and water heading toward the neighbor's garage. Anything I missed?
No, that is everything. Only please, tell them to come early, before the ice is more. Every morning is worse, because it is cold in the night.
I'll put that in the notes, that it refreezes overnight and mornings are the worst. Somebody should call you at that number if they have questions.
Okay. Thank you very much, Lorraine. I hope I don't need to call again.
I hope so too. Thanks for calling, Ms. Quintero. Take care on that sidewalk.
Yes, you too. Bye-bye.
